name: Duck 2
summary: Duck 1 plus an adaptive step size, trained from zero
what_changed: Same recipe as Duck 1, except the step size: after every brain update the learning rate is divided by 1.5 if the brain changed more than twice the target (0.01), or multiplied by 1.5 if it changed less than half of it (Rudin and others 2021).
why: Duck 1 collapsed after its best at 1.61M. A measurement run showed every update changing the brain 50 to 100 times more than PPO is designed for (approx_kl 0.5 to 1.1, safety limit hit by over 80% of moves), growing as the wobble shrank. Trained from zero with the same seed as Duck 1, so the two recipes can be compared fairly.
starts_from: zero (same seed and untrained brain as Duck 1)

runs.outcome: Slower start than Duck 1 (23 against 99 at 1.0M), then a jump to 395 at 1.5M and the best exam at 2.0M (557, 6 falls of 12). No collapse: after one dip to 151 at 2.25M it held between 381 and 448 up to 4.0M, where Duck 1 had fallen to 136. Each update changed the brain by about 0.015 (Duck 1: 0.5 to 1.1), the safety limit was hit by 20 to 24% of moves, and the learning rate fell from 0.0003 to about 0.00001

notes: Walks with alternating steps and about 96% one foot down once it is moving, using 15 to 18 J per metre, about half of Duck 1. Its weak point is the start: with some starting poses (a difference of about one degree per joint) it dives forward and falls within 0.6 s. The step size kept falling all run, so learning slowed down; a higher target change or a different rule could be the next recipe.

world_settings.notes: Duck 1, Duck 2 and Duck 2.1. They trained under an older forward reward, without the overshoot rule (going faster than asked did not lose points); this world has today's rule.
